propositions.statement: Let A and B be commutative semirings, S a multiplicative submonoid of A, and B an A-algebra which is a localization of A at S. Let T be an additive commutative monoid and A-module. Then the A-linear map f:T→B⊗_A T, f(t)=1⊗t, is a localized-module map at S: (i) multiplication by each s∈S on B⊗_A T is a unit in its semiring of A-linear endomorphisms; (ii) for every z∈B⊗_A T there exist t∈T and s∈S with sz=f(t); (iii) f(t₁)=f(t₂) implies that st₁=st₂ for some s∈S. A localization B at S means the images of S are units, every element has a numerator in A and denominator in S, and equality of images of two elements of A is killed by some element of S.

argument.text: H001 gives n>0 and the finite index set I. From H002 and H003, induction on t gives hy^t v=(λ-2t)y^t v and, for t≥1, xy^t v=t(λ-t+1)y^{t-1}v. Indeed h y=y h-2y gives the h step. For x, the base is xyv=yxv+hv=λv; if xy^t v=t(λ-t+1)y^{t-1}v, then xy^{t+1}v=yxy^t v+hy^t v=[t(λ-t+1)+λ-2t]y^t v=(t+1)(λ-t)y^t v. The t=0 h identity is hv=λv. Iterating the x identity, for 0≤i≤λ, gives x^i y^i v=i! λ(λ-1)⋯(λ-i+1)v≠0: every factor is a positive integer when i>0, and the empty product is 1 when i=0. Thus e_i≠0 for every i∈I.

produces.statement: For every s≥0, hy^s v=(λ-2s)y^s v, and for s≥1, xy^s v=s(λ-s+1)y^{s-1}v. Every e_i for i∈I is nonzero.

argument.text: Take arbitrary c:I→C and temporarily assume L1: ∑_{i∈I} c_i e_i=0. For each j∈I, apply ∏_{k∈I,k≠j}(h-(λ-2k)Id_V). F001 makes every summand except the j-th vanish, leaving c_j ∏_{k≠j}2(k-j)e_j=0. Its vector and scalar factors are nonzero over C, so c_j=0. Discharge L1; the family e is linearly independent. H002 gives dim_C V=n=card(I), so M003 makes its span all of V. Independence and spanning are precisely the basis conditions. The h formula at t=λ+1 has eigenvalue -λ-2. Expanding y^{λ+1}v in this basis and comparing coefficients in h gives [-λ-2-(λ-2i)] times its i-th coefficient equal to zero. These multipliers are nonzero for all i∈I, hence y^{λ+1}v=0. Further powers vanish by applying y.

argument.text: Divide the identities in F001 by i! and use F002 to obtain xe_0=0, xe_i=(λ-i+1)e_{i-1} for i≥1, ye_i=(i+1)e_{i+1} for i<λ, ye_λ=0, and he_i=(λ-2i)e_i. For any r≥0, iterate these formulas r times and divide by r!: for r≤i the x coefficient is (λ-i+1)⋯(λ-i+r)/r!=binom(λ-i+r,r), and for i+r≤λ the y coefficient is (i+1)⋯(i+r)/r!=binom(i+r,r). Outside those ranges the string has already hit zero, so the result is zero. The product ratios equal the integer binomial coefficients defined in D015: for natural A≥r, count ordered lists of r distinct elements of {1,...,A}. There are A(A-1)⋯(A-r+1) such lists, and each r-element subset occurs r! times, once per ordering. Hence binom(A,r)=A(A-1)⋯(A-r+1)/r!, also for r=0 by empty products. Substituting A=λ-i+r or A=i+r gives the displayed identities and integrality. At r=0 both products equal 1. This proves the full characteristic-zero coordinate statement.

argument.text: Define Qop=Y_λ X_λ. Test N001 on every e_k: X_λ kills k<λ and sends e_λ to e_0, while Y_λ e_0=e_λ; hence Qop=E_{λλ}. Likewise X_{λ-i}Qop=E_{iλ}, since X_{λ-i}e_λ=e_i. argument.text: For i∈I, E_ii maps M_R onto J_i e_i: its image is contained there by N002 and the coordinate formula, and it fixes every vector c e_i in that module. For i,j∈I, applying E_ij to c e_j proves J_j⊆J_i; interchanging indices proves equality. Thus J_i=J_0=J. Every vector in M_R is the sum of its E_ii projections, and the independence of e in N001 makes this sum direct. Therefore M_R=⊕_{i∈I}J e_i. Each summand is generated by the projections of the finite basis in N002. Since e_i≠0, multiplication by e_i identifies J with this summand, so J is finitely generated. argument.text: Define T=Q⊗_R J and μ:T→C by μ(q⊗c)=qc; balancing makes this a Q-linear map. Q is a localization of R at its nonzero elements: nonzero elements become units, every rational is a numerator/denominator with both in R (indeed integers suffice), and equality in Q is equality in the subring R, so the equality-killing condition holds with 1. M004 then says every z∈T satisfies sz=1⊗c for some c∈J and nonzero s∈R. Consequently μ(z)=c/s. If μ(z)=0, then c=0 in C, hence in J, so sz=0 and z=0 since s is invertible over Q. Thus μ is injective and its image is exactly the rational span of J. A finite R-generating list of J from F001 gives a finite Q-spanning list of T, because z=s^{-1}(1⊗c) and c is an R-combination of that list. Hence T is finite-dimensional.

argument.text: Define r=finrank_Q T. Tensoring the direct decomposition F001 yields a Q-linear equivalence Q⊗_R M_R≃∏_{i∈I}T. The inverse takes a tuple whose entries are finite sums of q⊗c to the sum of the tensors q⊗(c e_i). Coordinate extraction is R-linear; these prescriptions are balanced and additive, and their composites fix pure tensors and tuples of pure tensors, hence all finite sums, so they are inverse. M001 applied to the I-indexed R-basis of M_R supplied by N002 gives an I-indexed Q-basis of Q⊗_R M_R; M002 gives its dimension n. M008 gives freeness of T over Q, while F002 gives finite generation. Thus M006 gives dimension of ∏_I T equal to ∑_I r=nr, and M005 applied to the displayed equivalence gives n=nr. Since n=λ+1>0 by H001, r=1.

For each 1≤j≤k, write 1⊗g_j as q_j(1⊗a) and apply μ to get g_j=q_j a. Since g_j≠0, q_j≠0. argument.text: Choose the family q from F004. Each nonzero rational q_j can be written p^{ν_j}u_j with ν_j∈Z and u_j a unit in R. To see existence without assuming a rank-one ideal theorem, write the rational as a ratio of two nonzero integers. For a positive integer d, divide off p repeatedly while it divides d. This terminates: p≥2 by H001, so each division of a positive divisible integer strictly decreases it; equivalently induction on d supplies a largest nonnegative exponent with remaining positive factor not divisible by p. Apply this to the absolute values of numerator and denominator; keep their signs in the remaining factors. Subtract the two exponents to get ν_j. The remaining ratio and its inverse both have denominators not divisible by p, hence belong to R, giving the unit u_j. Applying this finite construction to all indices gives the families in F005.

argument.text: Choose b as in N003. Since K has characteristic p by H001, the kernel of Z→K is pZ: Euclidean division by p reduces any integer to a remainder 0≤s<p, and the definition of characteristic says no positive such remainder maps to zero. Consequently any integer d not divisible by p has nonzero image in K. Define ρ(a/d)=a_K/d_K on R. Equality of fractions is cross-multiplication in Z, hence in K; their denominators remain nonzero, proving well-definedness, additivity and multiplicativity. Thus ρ extends the integer map. Its kernel is pR, since a/d maps to zero exactly when p divides a. Reduction sends a/d modulo p to a times the inverse of d in F_p=Z/pZ, giving R/pR≃F_p with the natural inclusion F_p→K. The latter is injective by the same characteristic argument. Also X_1=x and Y_1=y preserve M by H004; H002 gives h=xy-yx, so h preserves M too. All induced lattice actions in D012 are therefore defined.

argument.text: Use N002 to identify M_R with R⊗_Z M. The first isomorphism sends m⊗c in M⊗_Z K to m⊗c in M_R⊗_R K, equivalently (1⊗m)⊗c. Its inverse sends (r⊗m)⊗c to m⊗ρ(r)c. Integer and R-balancing verify both maps, and their composites fix every pure tensor, hence all finite sums. For the second isomorphism send u⊗c to (u+pM_R)⊗c. The inverse sends (u+pM_R)⊗c to u⊗c; changing u by pz changes the result by z⊗pc=0. Balancing over F_p follows from F000 and the R-action through R/pR; the same pure tensor check shows inverse composites. These maps are K-linear and intertwine every induced R-linear lattice operator, as is checked on pure tensors.

argument.text: N003 says (b e_i) is an R-basis of M_R. Applying M001 with R→K makes the vectors 1⊗(b e_i) a K-basis of K⊗_R M_R. The flip of pure tensors, c⊗u↔u⊗c, is balanced and has itself as inverse, so it identifies this basis with (b e_i)⊗1 in M_R⊗_R K. Transporting through F001 defines β_i and proves β is a K-basis of V(K). Reduction of the R-basis modulo p is also a basis over F_p: its coordinates identify M_R with R^I and pM_R with (pR)^I, hence the quotient with (R/pR)^I. The second isomorphism in F001 therefore gives the same basis by reduction and extension. N001 applied to b e_i (b is a complex scalar) gives exactly xβ_0=0, xβ_i=(λ-i+1)β_{i-1}, yβ_i=(i+1)β_{i+1} for i<λ, yβ_λ=0, hβ_i=(λ-2i)β_i, with the boundary restrictions on x as in N001 and all coefficients mapped to K. Define ε_ij to be the matrix units for this basis. By N002, E_ij preserve M_R and hence induce these ε_ij, and their product identities persist by F001.

produces.statement: β is a K-basis of V(K) obtained from b e_i by the scalar-extension maps. Its operator formulas are xβ_0=0, xβ_i=(λ-i+1)β_{i-1} for i≥1, yβ_i=(i+1)β_{i+1} for i<λ, yβ_λ=0, hβ_i=(λ-2i)β_i, for i∈I. Induced E_ij are ε_ij, and ε_ij=ρ(binom(λ,j))^{-1} X_{λ-i}(Y_λX_λ)Y_{λ-j}, where X,Y here denote induced divided-power operators.

argument.text: For each 0≤r≤λ<p, M007 gives p not dividing r!, so its image in K is nonzero by F000. On the original lattice r!X_r=x^r and r!Y_r=y^r, and both sides preserve M. Thus after scalar extension X_r=(r!)^{-1}x^r and Y_r=(r!)^{-1}y^r in this range. N002 states binom(λ,j) is a unit in R; its image in K is a unit since ρ sends its inverse to an inverse. F002 therefore gives ε_ij=binom(λ,j)^{-1}X_{λ-i}(Y_λX_λ)Y_{λ-j}. A subspace invariant under x,y is invariant under their nonnegative powers, scalar multiples and compositions, so this formula proves its invariance under every ε_ij. All indices used here lie between 0 and λ. The argument works for any witness b allowed by N003, establishing the stated universal assertions.

applications.bindings: A=R, B=K with algebra map ρ, T=M_R, C=I, d_i=b e_i.
hypothesis_checks: R and K are commutative rings and F000 proves the ring map ρ.
M_R is an R-module by D008.
N003 and the witness b from S001 give the R-basis d_i=b e_i.
H001 gives prime p and 0≤r≤λ<p, so the source equivalence excludes p dividing r!.

locals.type: K-basis of V(K) indexed by I
locals.declaration: Choose the K-basis β with matrix-unit identities supplied by N004.
Define ε_ij to be the matrix units of the chosen basis β as in N004.
Fix an arbitrary K-linear subspace W of V(K).
In the nonzero branch choose w≠0 in W using F001 under L2.
Let c be the unique coordinate family of w in the basis β.
Choose j with c_j≠0; equivalently choose the index of a nonzero coordinate of w whose existence is in F001.

argument.text: Choose β and define ε as in N004; H001 gives n=λ+1>0, so I is nonempty. The basis vector β_0 is nonzero, proving V(K)≠0. Fix an arbitrary subspace W and assume L1: W is invariant under x,y,h. N004 then makes W invariant under every ε_ij. If W={0}, the desired alternative is already true. In the other branch assume L2: W≠{0}. By this assumption W has a nonzero vector; since β is a basis, such a vector has a nonzero coordinate. Record F001 to choose both a vector and an index in the next paragraph.

produces.statement: There exist a nonzero vector z∈W and an index t∈I such that the t-th coordinate of z in β is nonzero. Also W is invariant under every ε_{ii,jj} for ii,jj∈I.

argument.text: Choose the vector w and index j jointly from F001 and let w=∑_{i∈I}c_i β_i be its basis expansion, so c_j≠0. For every i∈I, the matrix-unit formula gives ε_ij w=c_j β_i∈W. Since K is a field, multiplication by c_j^{-1} gives β_i∈W. Every vector of V(K) is a K-linear combination of these basis vectors, so W=V(K). Thus in the nonzero branch the required alternative holds; discharge L2 and combine with the zero branch to get W={0} or W=V(K) under L1.

Discharge L1 and universally quantify the arbitrary W. Together with nonzeroness proved in S001 this proves the asserted subspace statement. For the Lie-algebra formulation, H004 and H002 give lattice preservation of x,y and h=xy-yx, so L(K) acts as defined; invariance under its generator span is equivalent, by linearity, to invariance under x,y,h. Hence the same statement is irreducibility as an L(K)-module. No algebraic closure of K was used. When λ=0, n=1 and all factorials and binomials in the route are 1; the proof remains valid. When p=2, H001 permits λ=0 or 1 and all factorials used have r<2. No distinctness of reduced h-eigenvalues was invoked.

full_target:
Let \(p\) be any prime, \(K\) any field of characteristic \(p\), and
\(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\)-module of highest weight \(\lambda\),
of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy

\[
[h,x]=2x,\qquad[h,y]=-2y,\qquad[x,y]=h.
\]

Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and
\(hv=\lambda v\). Let \(U_{\mathbb Z}\) be the integer subalgebra of
the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers
\(X_r=x^r/r!\), \(Y_r=y^r/r!\), for integers \(r\geq0\).
An **admissible lattice** \(M\subset V(\lambda)\) is a free abelian
subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under
\(U_{\mathbb Z}\). It is arbitrary, not necessarily the minimal lattice.

Put \(V(K)=M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\). The Lie algebra
\(L(K)=(\mathbb Zx+\mathbb Zy+\mathbb Zh)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\)
acts by the induced lattice operators. This is the Chevalley
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) construction also in characteristic 2.
Prove that \(V(K)\) is nonzero and every \(K\)-linear subspace
invariant under \(x,y,h\) is zero or all of \(V(K)\).
Both \(\lambda=0\) and \(p=2\) are included; \(K\) need not be
algebraically closed.
